arxiv-1410-4391.title: Multivariate Spearman’s ρ \rho for Aggregating Ranks Using Copulas
arxiv-1410-4391.creator: Justin Bedőcu@cua0.org, Cheng Soon Ongchengsoon.ong@anu.edu.au
arxiv-1410-4391.description: Abstract We study the problem of rank aggregation: given a set of ranked lists, we want to form a consensus ranking. Furthermore, we consider the case of extreme lists: i.e., only the rank of the best or worst elements are known. We impute missing ranks and generalise Spearman’s ρ \rho to extreme ranks.

arxiv-2202-00922.title: Search for Stellar Flybys in the Sco-Cen OB Association with the Gaia DR2 Journal: AJ
arxiv-2202-00922.creator: Yilun Ma (马逸伦), Robert J. De Rosa, Paul Kalas
arxiv-2202-00922.description: Abstract High-contrast imaging studies of debris disks have revealed a significant diversity in their morphologies, including large-scale asymmetries. Theories involving stellar flybys, an external source of gravitational disturbance, have offered a plausible explanation for the origin of these morphological variations. Our study is an experiment to gain empirical evidence that has been lacking from such theories.

arxiv-2202-08225.title: Why pseudo-complex General Relativity? and Applications
arxiv-2202-08225.creator: Peter O. Hess
arxiv-2202-08225.description: Abstract A brief discussion on the pseudo-complex General Relativity is presented. It is shown that this theory is a viable extension of GR, with deviations centered near to the event horizon. The theory introduces a dark energy accumulation, due to the coupling to the central mass.

arxiv-2207-05223.title: Bootstrapping a User-Centered Task-Oriented Dialogue System Thanks: Faculty advisors.
arxiv-2207-05223.creator: Shijie Chen, Ziru Chen, Xiang Deng, Ashley Lewis, Lingbo Mo, Samuel Stevens
arxiv-2207-05223.description: Abstract We present TacoBot , a task-oriented dialogue system built for the inaugural Alexa Prize TaskBot Challenge, which assists users in completing multi-step cooking and home improvement tasks. TacoBot is designed with a user-centered principle and aspires to deliver a collaborative and accessible dialogue experience.

arxiv-2303-13430.title: Medical diffusion on a budget: Textual Inversion for medical image generation
arxiv-2303-13430.creator: Bram de Wilde, Anindo Saha, Maarten de Rooij, Henkjan Huisman, Geert Litjens
arxiv-2303-13430.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bram de Wilde, Anindo Saha, Maarten de Rooij, Henkjan Huisman, Geert Litjens. Diffusion models for text-to-image generation, known for their efficiency, accessibility, and quality, have gained popularity. While inference with these systems on consumer-grade GPUs is increasingly feasible, training from scratch requires large captioned datasets and significant computational resources. In medical image generation, the limited availability of large, publicly accessible datasets with text reports poses challenges due to legal and ethical concerns.

arxiv-2402-04766.creator: Alena Jarolímová, Jaroslav Hron
arxiv-2402-04766.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alena Jarolímová, Jaroslav Hron. One of the crucial aspects of patient-specific blood flow simulations is to specify material parameters and boundary conditions. The choice of boundary conditions can have a substantial impact on the character of the flow. While no-slip is the most popular wall boundary condition, some amount of slip, which determines how much fluid is allowed to flow along the wall, might be beneficial for better agreement with flow patterns in medical images.

arxiv-2403-10821.title: H3-Mapping: Quasi-Heterogeneous Feature Grids for Real-time Dense Mapping Using Hierarchical Hybrid Representation
arxiv-2403-10821.creator: Chenxing Jiang, Yiming Luo, Boyu Zhou, Shaojie Shen
arxiv-2403-10821.description: Abstract In recent years, implicit online dense mapping methods have achieved high-quality reconstruction results, showcasing great potential in robotics, AR/VR, and digital twins applications. However, existing methods struggle with slow texture modeling which limits their real-time performance. To address these limitations, we propose a NeRF-based dense mapping method that enables faster and higher-quality reconstruction.

arxiv-2502-15703.title: An introduction to tensors for path signatures
arxiv-2502-15703.creator: Jack Beda, Gonçalo dos Reis and Nikolas Tapia
arxiv-2502-15703.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jack Beda, Gonçalo dos Reis and Nikolas Tapia. We present a fit-for-purpose introduction to tensors and their operations. It is envisaged to help the reader become acquainted with its underpinning concepts for the study of path signatures. The text includes exercises, solutions and many intuitive explanations. The material discusses direct sums and tensor products as two possible operations that make the Cartesian product of vectors spaces a vector space. The difference lies in linear Vs.

pmc-10704769.creator: Zheng Minjie, Xie Zhijuan, Shi Xinxin, Bai Xinzhu, Qu Shan
pmc-10704769.description: BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) often leads to an impaired Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) in many patients.
